item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio — Tue Sep 8, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketche

item.title: North Pocono Happy Hike — Sun Sep 13, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us on this point-to-point hike, tracing historic Rail lines and other interesting and random stuff through the Northern tier of the Pocono Mountains. We meet on the Old State Road at the trailhead for the North Pocono Rail Trail. From here, we will head West and shuttle with his few cars as possible to our start. from there, we will meander along some abandoned railroad beds, as well as some old turnpike routes, with only very short bits of road between. There may be one bridge on the way those with height issues won't like. Aside from that, the route is almost entirely clear and easy. Some might have uneven service, and only about 3 mi is improved surface. Everyone should come prepared with everything they need because we are only passing by one location where we can refill on any food or drink.Distance is about 15 mi. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
Source: Meetup: Metrotrails Hiking

item.title: Tech Talks: Library Tools (BCCLS, Libby, Hoopla) — Mon Sep 14, 4:00 PM — Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: Library Tools (BCCLS, Libby, Hoopla)
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:

Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. item.title: 'The Shoes' Play Reading — Thu Sep 24, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Come enjoy a reading of The Shoes before it hits the New York Theater Festival this winter!
The Shoes follows the story of Kent Warner, the man who changed the course of Hollywood history when he discovered Judy Garland's iconic ruby slippers from The Wizard of Oz hidden away in storage. Yet, behind the glitz and glamour of showbiz, Kent struggled with his identity, a sense of belonging, and the search for love—often using his passion for classic cinema to escape his own reality.
In a world of good and bad witches, of empty heads and aching hearts, Kent ultimately proved to be the courage at the center of it all.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Jersey Central Farewell Summer Shore Hike — Sun Sep 27, 8:45 AM
item.description: Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point hike in the north NJ shore region. The theme of this one is of course the end of Summer, but also the historic Central Railroad of New Jersey. The CNJ served a lot of shore points, and it's always fun to visit them on the hikes. So, for this one, we will focus on some of these rights of ways, including ones on the beach. After meeting at the end point. Lot C at Sandy Hook, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to a point south of Red Bank where there was a junction with the New York and Long Branch line. The CNJ had a line to the east from here, which served Port Monmouth and continued east to a junction with the Seashore Branch. We will trace this as closely as possible. Some bits of it are now trail, but they are very short. Some bits are now parking lots, gas lines, or roads. The route will take us through the raceway area, and then out toward the shore line. item.description: Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women What can poetry say about our bodies that ordinary language can’t? How can our bodily experiences open new paths for our writing? In this generative workshop for women and nonbinary writers, Barbara O’Dair – poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series – leads the group through readings, discussion, and writing exercises, using prompts to reveal fresh language, unexpected stories, and adventurous forms, and drawing from subjects such as body image, sexuality, desire, gender, illness, health, and aging. item.title: How Money Became God: Rethinking Wealth and Greed in Modern Society with Paul Vigna — Wed Nov 11, 2:00 PM — Glen Ridge Free Public Library
item.description:
Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society?
In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today’s global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today’s secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void.

item.title: Fire, Passion, and Heritage: Native American and Mexican Cooking with Chef Pyet DeSpain — Thu Nov 12, 2:00 PM — Glen Ridge Free Public Library
item.description:
Prepare your palate for a vibrant culinary journey with star chef Pyet DeSpain, the inaugural winner of Gordon Ramsay’s hit television competition Next Level Chef, as she presents her debut cookbook, Rooted in Fire: A Celebration of Native American and Mexican Cooking.
Pyet DeSpain rose to prominence as the first winner of Gordon Ramsey’s Fox television show Next Level Chef. Now, in her debut cookbook, she shares the joy of cooking fueled by her burning passion for Native American and Mexican American cuisine.
Pyet shows you how to incorporate a delicious range of key ingredients—from venison, dandelion greens, to sunchokes, bison, and native berries—into more than sixty fusion dishes. Family and friends will be excited to gather around the table to enjoy sweet and savory food such as:
Three Sisters Salad Bison and Sweet Corn Soup Fry Bread Mexican Chocolate & Mezcal Cake Corn Silk and Honey Tea Wojapi BBQ Sauce
Rooted in Fire is far more than just a collection of recipes

After you know the basics of Mah Jongg, and would like to play the game with other Mah Jongg players, please register for the weekly Thursday or the weekly Saturday "Mah Jongg Meetup".
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306
